- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate late-period spikes (especially >85) when sentiment is strong and rising — model fails to capture tail risk or policy-driven surges.
- Lag in correction after sharp price drops — model often holds low prices too long, ignoring sentiment reversal signals.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overcorrects after strong upward moves, underestimating sustained momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.18), model underreacts — fails to anticipate downward pressure or policy interventions.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently underestimates final 5–7 days when sentiment is volatile — adjust downward by 1–2% for high-sentiment volatility windows.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes — model reacts too quickly to sentiment peaks, then overcorrects, missing sustained rally.
